column1: # The arbitrations: one row per disagreement class the gap report can raise.
# Two decoders, one encoding, two answers.  The contract's step 5 says a
# disagreement is ARBITRATED to the CORRECT output, never resolved by picking
# a side and trusting it, so each row below decides on the merits and says
# which side the merits went to.  A row is NOT a claim that the other side is
# a defect: it is a claim about what the encoding does.
#   isa       the ISA the class was measured on
#   rule      the QEMU decode rule the class sits on, or #undecoded when the
#             bytes reached no rule at all
#   qemu      the generic opcode QEMU's word maps to
#   capstone  the generic opcode the incumbent names
#   verdict   QEMU | CAPSTONE -- which side the arbitration went to
#   state     SETTLED      the tree already publishes the arbitrated answer
#             COVERAGE-PATH the arbitrated answer is not published yet and the
#                          remedy is named in the reason
#   reason    the merits, in one sentence
# THE KEY INCLUDES THE RULE ON PURPOSE.  A class keyed only on the pair of
# opcodes grows silently: x86's BITMANIP-vs-TEST class was one row when B1
# ruled it and thirty-six at a five-times-larger corpus, and a rule joining an
# already-ruled pair would have been counted as ruled without anyone reading
# it.  A new rule in an old class is a new arbitration.
